changes.reason: Record the design rules the product documents state, anchored to the operations they govern

after.text: Human review is required before export. No proposed value reaches the completed PDF without a person having decided it.

meta.title: Nothing is exported that a human did not decide
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:337, stated as a product principle: "Human review is required before export." Accepted because the PRD records it as confirmed scope rather than an open decision.

after.text: Export is refused while any required review item is unresolved, and again until final confirmation is given. Resolution and confirmation are two separate conditions, not one.

meta.title: Export is gated on resolution and then on confirmation
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:158 "Prevent export until all required review items are resolved and final confirmation is given"; PRD:129.

after.text: The export gate is enforced on the server. A browser that is bypassed still cannot export a job with an unresolved required item.

meta.title: The export gate survives a bypassed browser
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:261 "The server blocks export when a required review item is unresolved, even if the browser is bypassed."

after.text: A suggestion the administrator rejected or deliberately omitted does not appear in the exported PDF. Omission is a recorded decision, not an absence of one.

meta.title: A rejected suggestion leaves no trace in the output
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:259; the recorded-state requirement is PRD:156.

after.text: Confidence is information shown to the reviewer. In the MVP no confidence value, however high, permits skipping review.

meta.title: Confidence informs review and never replaces it
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:230 "Confidence is information for review, not permission to bypass review in the MVP."

after.text: Every proposed value identifies the supporting document and page it came from.

meta.title: Every proposal names its document and page
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:255; the extraction-side requirement is PRD:152.

after.text: A value whose provenance cannot be shown cannot be accepted as an AI suggestion. The administrator may still type the value manually, but not accept it as extracted.

meta.title: A value without provenance cannot be accepted as a suggestion
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:180 "unsupported provenance blocks acceptance as an AI suggestion". The second sentence is an assistant reading of the accept/correct distinction at PRD:156 and is open to correction.

after.text: Candidate values are mapped only onto target fields that were actually detected, and a source value is never invented. Fabricating a missing detail is forbidden outright.

meta.title: The system never invents a value or a field
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:153 and PRD:228 "AI must not fabricate missing details, silently select between conflicting sources, sign, consent, or autonomously submit the form."

after.text: Conflicts, expired evidence, declarations and unsupported fields are visibly flagged and cannot pass silently. Silence is the failure mode the product is designed against.

meta.title: No exception may pass without being seen
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:257. The second sentence is an assistant characterisation of why the rule exists.

after.text: When two documents propose materially different values, both sources are shown and the administrator selects or enters the correct one. The system never picks a winner, and neither source gains standing from being uploaded later.

meta.title: A conflict is presented, never resolved by the system
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:169; the upload-order clause is EXAMPLES:67-69 "neither value is treated as high-confidence merely because one source was uploaded later".

after.text: A credential that appears expired or does not satisfy the requested field is flagged clearly. Extraction of a credential is never treated as approval of it.

meta.title: Extracting a credential is not approving it
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:170 "Flag clearly; never treat extraction as approval."

after.text: Signatures, declarations, consent and agreement to site terms are never auto-completed. The field is left for manual action and agreement is never inferred or generated.

meta.title: The system never signs, consents or agrees
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:157 and PRD:171.

after.text: A supporting document asserting that the worker already agreed to site terms does not entitle FormFlow to fill the declaration. The claim is evidence about the world, not an instruction to the system.

meta.title: A source document claiming consent does not grant it
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: EXAMPLES:61-62 "Agree To Site Terms: Yes, which a source document may claim and FormFlow must still refuse to accept on its own (FR-012)." The second sentence is an assistant framing.

after.text: A field type or layout that cannot be completed reliably is explained to the administrator and left for manual completion outside FormFlow. A target that cannot be handled fails clearly rather than producing an unreliable form.

meta.title: An unsupported field is refused with an explanation, not guessed
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:172 and PRD:313.

after.text: File limits, known field IDs, allowed value types, required review states and export gating are enforced by deterministic code. The model is not trusted to enforce any of them.

meta.title: Deterministic code owns every limit the model could violate
meta.author: speaker unknown

after.text: The model's permitted scope is interpretation: field labels, document text, and likely source-to-target relationships. It has no authority to decide, approve or submit.

meta.title: The model interprets and never decides
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:224 lists the permitted scope; PRD:228 lists the forbidden actions. Paraphrase joining the two.

after.text: The completed form is a separate new PDF. The uploaded target file is never modified.

meta.title: The blank target is never written to
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:159 and PRD:75.

after.text: Until the pilot security gate is approved, only synthetic or formally approved redacted documents may be processed. Customer documents must not enter the repository, issues, CI or support channels at any point.

meta.title: Real personal information is not permitted yet
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:189; the channel restriction is EXAMPLES:4-6; the no-customer-forms rule is PRD:245.

after.text: Only what is required to process and support the current job is stored. No persistent worker or company profile is created.

meta.title: The MVP stores a job, not a person
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:192 and PRD:161. Contradicted in practice by EXAMPLES:96-107, which describes approving and reusing a worker profile.

after.text: Logs carry request, job, document and organisation identifiers only. Document bytes, OCR text, extracted values, prompts, credentials, personal fields and signed URLs never appear in them.

meta.title: Logs carry identifiers and nothing about the person
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:83, restated as an acceptance criterion at PRD:269 and a transport rule at PRD:191.

after.text: Raw files never pass through Vercel in staging or production. Browsers upload directly to the private quarantine bucket using ten-minute V4 grants.

meta.title: Uploaded bytes never touch the application server
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:11; bucket access rules at SECOPS:12.

after.text: A row's own retentionExpiresAt is a hard maximum with no grace of any kind. Shortening a retention setting shortens live attempts too, and can never lengthen one.

meta.title: The retention deadline admits no grace, even for a running attempt
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:30 and SECOPS:32.

after.text: An admitted live worker can never read an input retention has already deleted, because the capability is re-taken as a compare-and-set before every object read and an attempt holding under a minute of lease stops, writes nothing, and records job.processing_lease_lost.

meta.title: A running worker cannot read a file retention has deleted
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:32.

after.text: The MVP is intentionally a single-job document workflow, not a worker-management system, document-management platform, portal-submission tool or autonomous agent. Its purpose is to prove that site-access forms can be prepared materially faster without reducing human control.

meta.title: The MVP proves a speed claim, it does not become a platform
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:25. Thirteen explicit exclusions follow at PRD:81-107.

after.text: Source files are deleted 24 hours after job completion and target and output files after 7 days. The PRD marks these as provisional maximums requiring Blake to make them configurable and Marno to confirm them before real-data use.

meta.title: The retention windows are provisional, not settled
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:193 uses the word "Provisional"; PRD:347 lists retention approval as an open decision owned by Marno and the pilot. SECOPS:27-28 states different windows as settled operational fact, anchored to a profile decision rather than to job completion.

after.text: At least 95% of proposed ordinary field values exactly match expected values on the versioned synthetic benchmark, and no critical identity field has a silently accepted incorrect value because all values require review.

meta.title: Ninety-five percent exact match on the synthetic benchmark
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:265. Left proposed because the PRD does not partition ordinary from critical identity fields, and because EXAMPLES:111-112 and README:32-33 both deny that the shipped pack is the accuracy benchmark this target refers to.

after.text: Median task time is at least 70% lower than the manual baseline for the same benchmark, measured after the pilot team records that baseline.

meta.title: Seventy percent faster than the manual baseline
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:267. Left proposed because the baseline has not been recorded: PRD:344 still lists it as an open input and PRD:319 records the ungrounded-target risk.

after.text: Application data, document storage and processing are hosted in Australian regions. The PRD states this as a preference where supported; the security document states it as a requirement, pinning Vercel functions to syd1 and Supabase, Cloud Run, Document AI and Vertex AI to australia-southeast1.

meta.title: Australian hosting is a preference in one document and a requirement in the other
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:195 "Prefer Australian regions ... where supported" against SECOPS:7-9 "must". Recorded as one claim carrying the discrepancy rather than two, so the disagreement stays visible.

after.text: Up to five supporting documents per job is sufficient for a real site-access pack. A sixth is blocked with a clear explanation.

meta.title: Five supporting documents is enough for a real pack
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:57 and PRD:253 state the limit; PRD:331 records it as a confirmed assumption. Left proposed because no document offers evidence that real packs fit in five files.

fill-job.text: One administrator's attempt to complete one blank target form for one worker, holding status, timestamps and the files uploaded to it. A job is an attempt, not a worker record: the MVP creates no persistent worker or company profile.

meta.title: Fill job
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:208 defines it as status, timestamps and relationship to uploaded files; PRD:25 states the MVP is intentionally a single-job document workflow. SECOPS:32 adds lease and lock semantics to the same row.

target-form.text: The blank site-access PDF an administrator must complete, one per job. It is read and never written: the completed form is a separate output file.

meta.title: Target form
meta.author: assistant

supporting-document.text: A worker or company document uploaded as evidence for one job, up to five per job, in PDF, JPG or PNG. It is evidence for one attempt, not a stored record: it is deleted within the retention window.

meta.title: Supporting document
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:57, PRD:59, PRD:121, PRD:212; retention at PRD:193 and SECOPS:27.

target-field.text: One completable location detected on the target form, with its name, type, location and required status where known. Whether a field is required is not always determinable, and export gating depends on it.

meta.title: Target field
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:214 records required status "where known"; PRD:151 requires unsupported targets to be reported clearly.

candidate-value.text: A value extracted from a supporting document, carrying the document and page it came from and the extraction method. A candidate is not yet an answer: it becomes one only through a suggestion a human resolves.

meta.title: Candidate value
meta.author: assistant

suggestion.text: The unit a human acts on: a proposed mapping of a candidate value onto a target field, together with its review state, its final value and the user's recorded decision. Distinct from the candidate value it carries.

meta.title: Suggestion
meta.author: assistant

review-status.text: The classification carried by every suggestion: supported evidence, missing, conflict, expired or unsuitable, declaration, or unsupported. There is no unstatused suggestion, and the status determines what a human must do before export.

meta.title: Review status
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:154 and the six-row table at PRD:165-172.

declaration-field.text: A target field asking the administrator to attest, agree or sign. FormFlow must never propose a value for it, even when a supporting document claims the person already agreed.

meta.title: Declaration field
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:157 and PRD:171; EXAMPLES:61-62 gives the concrete case where a source claims "Agree To Site Terms: Yes" and FormFlow must still refuse it.

completed-pdf.text: The separate generated PDF containing only the values a human resolved. It is a new file; the original target is never altered.

meta.title: Completed PDF
meta.author: assistant

administrator.text: The human role that uploads the pack, resolves every suggestion and confirms export. An administrator, mobilisation coordinator or contracts officer. This anchor denotes a role, not a login or a session.

meta.title: Administrator
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:41, PRD:206.

organisation.text: The tenancy boundary for closed beta. One active membership per user, with isolation enforced at the database row level. It appears in the security model and the logging rules but not in the PRD's data model.

meta.title: Organisation
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: SECOPS:23, SECOPS:76, SECOPS:83, SECOPS:89. Absent from PRD:204-220, which models identity only as "User/session".

processing-capability.text: A random expiring lease minted for one processing attempt, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, re-taken as a compare-and-set before every read of an uploaded object, and revoked on cancellation or any terminal outcome. It is what makes a live worker unable to read a file retention has already deleted.

meta.title: Processing capability
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: SECOPS:19, SECOPS:31, SECOPS:32.

retention-action.text: The evidence row written for each attempted deletion of a stored document. It is proof that a deletion was attempted and what happened, separate from the file being gone.

meta.title: Retention action
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: SECOPS:29.

worker-profile.text: A reusable store of an approved worker's fields, carried across jobs so a returning worker's details can be proposed for reuse. The examples treat it as a live entity an administrator approves; the PRD lists it as excluded from the MVP. Whether it exists is unsettled.

meta.title: Worker profile
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: EXAMPLES:96-107 describes approving its creation and reusing its fields; PRD:83 excludes it and PRD:161 states "no reusable worker profile is created". SECOPS:27 anchors supporting-document deletion to "the profile decision".

create-job.text: Bring a new isolated form-completion job into existence for one administrator and one target form.

meta.title: Create job
meta.author: assistant

upload-pack.text: Submit one target form and up to five supporting documents to a job. Type, size and readability are validated before processing, and files go directly to a private bucket rather than through the application server. Distinct from starting processing.

meta.title: Upload the pack
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:147, PRD:149, PRD:150, PRD:253; SECOPS:11.

start-processing.text: Begin one extraction attempt on a job's uploaded files under a minted capability. An attempt whose inputs have already passed their retention deadline is refused rather than started.

meta.title: Start processing
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:123, PRD:196, PRD:197; SECOPS:31.

detect-fields.text: Identify the completable fields on the target form and their type and location, and report clearly any target the system cannot support. Distinct from extracting values.

meta.title: Detect target fields
meta.author: assistant

extract-values.text: Read candidate values out of the supporting documents, each carrying the document and page it came from. Extraction is interpretation of evidence, never approval of it.

meta.title: Extract candidate values
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:152; the never-approval constraint is stated at PRD:170.

match-candidate.text: Propose a candidate value for a known target field. Mapping is restricted to fields that were detected; inventing a source value is forbidden.

meta.title: Match a candidate to a field
meta.author: assistant

classify-suggestion.text: Assign every suggestion one of the six review statuses. This is the step that makes a conflict, an expiry or a declaration visible rather than silently resolved.

meta.title: Classify a suggestion
meta.author: assistant

resolve-suggestion.text: A human accepts, edits, rejects or deliberately omits one suggestion, and the decision is recorded. Only the resolved value reaches the output. Performed by the administrator, never by the system.

meta.title: Resolve a suggestion
meta.author: assistant

attest-declaration.text: A person records agreement to a declaration or consent field. Only a human may perform it; no extraction, however confident, substitutes for it.

meta.title: Attest a declaration
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:157, PRD:171; EXAMPLES:61-62. The repository commit 54f80ab "Let a person attest a declaration the matcher never proposed" indicates this was implemented separately from ordinary resolution.

confirm-export.text: The administrator gives final confirmation that the job may be exported. It is refused while any required review item is unresolved, and the refusal is enforced on the server, not only in the browser.

meta.title: Confirm export
meta.author: assistant

generate-pdf.text: Write the resolved values into a new PDF that preserves the target's layout. The original target file is not modified.

meta.title: Generate the completed PDF
meta.author: assistant

retry-job.text: Start a further attempt on a job whose previous attempt failed. Retry is only meaningful while the job's inputs still exist; once retention has deleted them the correct outcome is a refusal that explains re-upload, not a retry.

meta.title: Retry a failed job
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: PRD:160; SECOPS:33 describes the expired-input terminal path and the "replacement-upload sentence".

sweep-retention.text: Delete stored documents whose retention window has passed and write a RetentionAction for each attempt. Triggered by an external daily schedule pointed at the worker origin, not by the application itself.

meta.title: Sweep retention
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: SECOPS:27-29, SECOPS:38-58, SECOPS:69-70.

human-review-before-export.text: Human review is required before export. No proposed value reaches the completed PDF without a person having decided it.

meta.title: Nothing is exported that a human did not decide
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:337, stated as a product principle: "Human review is required before export." Accepted because the PRD records it as confirmed scope rather than an open decision.

export-blocked-until-resolved.text: Export is refused while any required review item is unresolved, and again until final confirmation is given. Resolution and confirmation are two separate conditions, not one.

meta.title: Export is gated on resolution and then on confirmation
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:158 "Prevent export until all required review items are resolved and final confirmation is given"; PRD:129.

server-enforces-export-gate.text: The export gate is enforced on the server. A browser that is bypassed still cannot export a job with an unresolved required item.

meta.title: The export gate survives a bypassed browser
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:261 "The server blocks export when a required review item is unresolved, even if the browser is bypassed."

rejected-values-never-exported.text: A suggestion the administrator rejected or deliberately omitted does not appear in the exported PDF. Omission is a recorded decision, not an absence of one.

meta.title: A rejected suggestion leaves no trace in the output
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:259; the recorded-state requirement is PRD:156.

confidence-is-not-permission.text: Confidence is information shown to the reviewer. In the MVP no confidence value, however high, permits skipping review.

meta.title: Confidence informs review and never replaces it
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:230 "Confidence is information for review, not permission to bypass review in the MVP."

every-value-cites-source.text: Every proposed value identifies the supporting document and page it came from.

meta.title: Every proposal names its document and page
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:255; the extraction-side requirement is PRD:152.

unsupported-provenance-blocks-acceptance.text: A value whose provenance cannot be shown cannot be accepted as an AI suggestion. The administrator may still type the value manually, but not accept it as extracted.

meta.title: A value without provenance cannot be accepted as a suggestion
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:180 "unsupported provenance blocks acceptance as an AI suggestion". The second sentence is an assistant reading of the accept/correct distinction at PRD:156 and is open to correction.

never-invent-a-value.text: Candidate values are mapped only onto target fields that were actually detected, and a source value is never invented. Fabricating a missing detail is forbidden outright.

meta.title: The system never invents a value or a field
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:153 and PRD:228 "AI must not fabricate missing details, silently select between conflicting sources, sign, consent, or autonomously submit the form."

exceptions-cannot-pass-silently.text: Conflicts, expired evidence, declarations and unsupported fields are visibly flagged and cannot pass silently. Silence is the failure mode the product is designed against.

meta.title: No exception may pass without being seen
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:257. The second sentence is an assistant characterisation of why the rule exists.

conflict-shows-both-sources.text: When two documents propose materially different values, both sources are shown and the administrator selects or enters the correct one. The system never picks a winner, and neither source gains standing from being uploaded later.

meta.title: A conflict is presented, never resolved by the system
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:169; the upload-order clause is EXAMPLES:67-69 "neither value is treated as high-confidence merely because one source was uploaded later".

expiry-flagged-never-approved.text: A credential that appears expired or does not satisfy the requested field is flagged clearly. Extraction of a credential is never treated as approval of it.

meta.title: Extracting a credential is not approving it
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:170 "Flag clearly; never treat extraction as approval."

declarations-never-auto-completed.text: Signatures, declarations, consent and agreement to site terms are never auto-completed. The field is left for manual action and agreement is never inferred or generated.

meta.title: The system never signs, consents or agrees
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:157 and PRD:171.

declaration-claimed-by-source-still-refu.text: A supporting document asserting that the worker already agreed to site terms does not entitle FormFlow to fill the declaration. The claim is evidence about the world, not an instruction to the system.

meta.title: A source document claiming consent does not grant it
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: EXAMPLES:61-62 "Agree To Site Terms: Yes, which a source document may claim and FormFlow must still refuse to accept on its own (FR-012)." The second sentence is an assistant framing.

unsupported-field-explained-not-guessed.text: A field type or layout that cannot be completed reliably is explained to the administrator and left for manual completion outside FormFlow. A target that cannot be handled fails clearly rather than producing an unreliable form.

meta.title: An unsupported field is refused with an explanation, not guessed
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:172 and PRD:313.

deterministic-code-enforces-limits.text: File limits, known field IDs, allowed value types, required review states and export gating are enforced by deterministic code. The model is not trusted to enforce any of them.

meta.title: Deterministic code owns every limit the model could violate
meta.author: speaker unknown

ai-interprets-only.text: The model's permitted scope is interpretation: field labels, document text, and likely source-to-target relationships. It has no authority to decide, approve or submit.

meta.title: The model interprets and never decides
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:224 lists the permitted scope; PRD:228 lists the forbidden actions. Paraphrase joining the two.

original-target-unaltered.text: The completed form is a separate new PDF. The uploaded target file is never modified.

meta.title: The blank target is never written to
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:159 and PRD:75.

synthetic-documents-only.text: Until the pilot security gate is approved, only synthetic or formally approved redacted documents may be processed. Customer documents must not enter the repository, issues, CI or support channels at any point.

meta.title: Real personal information is not permitted yet
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:189; the channel restriction is EXAMPLES:4-6; the no-customer-forms rule is PRD:245.

no-persistent-profiles.text: Only what is required to process and support the current job is stored. No persistent worker or company profile is created.

meta.title: The MVP stores a job, not a person
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:192 and PRD:161. Contradicted in practice by EXAMPLES:96-107, which describes approving and reusing a worker profile.

no-document-content-in-logs.text: Logs carry request, job, document and organisation identifiers only. Document bytes, OCR text, extracted values, prompts, credentials, personal fields and signed URLs never appear in them.

meta.title: Logs carry identifiers and nothing about the person
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:83, restated as an acceptance criterion at PRD:269 and a transport rule at PRD:191.

raw-files-bypass-vercel.text: Raw files never pass through Vercel in staging or production. Browsers upload directly to the private quarantine bucket using ten-minute V4 grants.

meta.title: Uploaded bytes never touch the application server
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:11; bucket access rules at SECOPS:12.

retention-hard-max-no-grace.text: A row's own retentionExpiresAt is a hard maximum with no grace of any kind. Shortening a retention setting shortens live attempts too, and can never lengthen one.

meta.title: The retention deadline admits no grace, even for a running attempt
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:30 and SECOPS:32.

lease-prevents-reading-deleted-input.text: An admitted live worker can never read an input retention has already deleted, because the capability is re-taken as a compare-and-set before every object read and an attempt holding under a minute of lease stops, writes nothing, and records job.processing_lease_lost.

meta.title: A running worker cannot read a file retention has deleted
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: SECOPS:32.

single-job-not-worker-system.text: The MVP is intentionally a single-job document workflow, not a worker-management system, document-management platform, portal-submission tool or autonomous agent. Its purpose is to prove that site-access forms can be prepared materially faster without reducing human control.

meta.title: The MVP proves a speed claim, it does not become a platform
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:25. Thirteen explicit exclusions follow at PRD:81-107.

retention-windows-provisional.text: Source files are deleted 24 hours after job completion and target and output files after 7 days. The PRD marks these as provisional maximums requiring Blake to make them configurable and Marno to confirm them before real-data use.

meta.title: The retention windows are provisional, not settled
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:193 uses the word "Provisional"; PRD:347 lists retention approval as an open decision owned by Marno and the pilot. SECOPS:27-28 states different windows as settled operational fact, anchored to a profile decision rather than to job completion.

accuracy-target-95.text: At least 95% of proposed ordinary field values exactly match expected values on the versioned synthetic benchmark, and no critical identity field has a silently accepted incorrect value because all values require review.

meta.title: Ninety-five percent exact match on the synthetic benchmark
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:265. Left proposed because the PRD does not partition ordinary from critical identity fields, and because EXAMPLES:111-112 and README:32-33 both deny that the shipped pack is the accuracy benchmark this target refers to.

time-saving-target-70.text: Median task time is at least 70% lower than the manual baseline for the same benchmark, measured after the pilot team records that baseline.

meta.title: Seventy percent faster than the manual baseline
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:267. Left proposed because the baseline has not been recorded: PRD:344 still lists it as an open input and PRD:319 records the ungrounded-target risk.

australian-region.text: Application data, document storage and processing are hosted in Australian regions. The PRD states this as a preference where supported; the security document states it as a requirement, pinning Vercel functions to syd1 and Supabase, Cloud Run, Document AI and Vertex AI to australia-southeast1.

meta.title: Australian hosting is a preference in one document and a requirement in the other
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:195 "Prefer Australian regions ... where supported" against SECOPS:7-9 "must". Recorded as one claim carrying the discrepancy rather than two, so the disagreement stays visible.

five-supporting-documents.text: Up to five supporting documents per job is sufficient for a real site-access pack. A sixth is blocked with a clear explanation.

meta.title: Five supporting documents is enough for a real pack
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: PRD:57 and PRD:253 state the limit; PRD:331 records it as a confirmed assumption. Left proposed because no document offers evidence that real packs fit in five files.

pilot-runbook.text: docs/PILOT-RUNBOOK.md, 46KB, last modified 2026-09-01. Verbatim: "This document records what is actually deployed for the private pilot... Every name, region, identity and command below was taken from the running deployment, not from a plan." Records the Vercel project formflow-preview in syd1, the Cloud Run worker formflow-worker in australia-southeast1, the Supabase project in ap-southeast-2, three GCS buckets, Cloud Tasks and Cloud Scheduler. It is linked from neither README.md nor docs/README.md.

meta.title: Pilot runbook, the live deployment record
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: File at docs/PILOT-RUNBOOK.md. Assessed as the most current and reliable status document in the repository.

Header verbatim: "Status date: 25 July 2026" and "Release status: local implementation in progress; not deployed, not security-approved". meta.title: Implementation handover, an architectural intent document
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: File at docs/IMPLEMENTATION-HANDOVER.md. Approximately seven weeks and sixty-three commits behind the working tree; contradicted on deployment status, branch name, test counts, browser suites, MFA, provider choice, worker database scoping and MVP scope.

pilot-is-deployed.text: A private pilot deployment exists and is reachable: the Vercel web plane formflow-preview in syd1, a Cloud Run worker in australia-southeast1, Supabase in ap-southeast-2, three private GCS buckets, Cloud Tasks and a daily Cloud Scheduler retention sweep.

meta.title: The pilot is deployed and reachable
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: docs/PILOT-RUNBOOK.md:20-27 records every name and region as taken from the running deployment. Independently checked during this session: GET https://formflow-preview.vercel.app/api/health returned 200 and /fill returned a 307 to authentication.

pilot-runs-the-fake-provider.text: The deployed pilot extracts nothing. Document AI and Vertex AI are not deployed and the pilot runs EXTRACTION_PROVIDER=fake, an in-process fixture that returns predetermined values.

meta.title: The deployed pilot does no real extraction
meta.author: speaker unknown
meta.provenance: docs/PILOT-RUNBOOK.md:31-34: "the provider-dependent services - Document AI and Vertex AI - are not deployed: extraction runs on the in-process fixture provider (EXTRACTION_PROVIDER=fake)".

accuracy-never-measured-on-a-real-provid.text: No accuracy figure for a real extraction provider exists. The only recorded accuracy run scores 11 of 11 against the fake provider, which returns the same values the expectation file lists, and the shipped confidence version is literally named uncalibrated-v1.

meta.title: Extraction accuracy has never been measured
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: web/.benchmark/accuracy-fake.json records provider "fake", denominator 11, matched 11; web/.benchmark/clean-fill-baseline.json lists the same values. docs/IMPLEMENTATION-HANDOVER.md:197 gives confidenceVersion as uncalibrated-v1 and :221 marks accuracy evaluation Absent with "Confidence is deliberately uncalibrated".

review-workspace-built.text: The side-by-side review workspace is built and working: the target PDF renders through pdf.js with page navigation and zoom, the current field's stored region is outlined on the page and scrolled into view, and the evidence pane distinguishes available, retention-deleted, unexpectedly-absent and no-source states.

meta.title: The review workspace is built, including region highlighting
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: web/src/app/(app)/fill/[jobId]/review/target-preview.tsx:23-204 and :174-186; evidence states at web/src/lib/documents/evidence.ts:110-146 and review/page.tsx:194-244. Contradicts docs/IMPLEMENTATION-HANDOVER.md:204, which marks region highlighting partial.

export-gate-built.text: The export gate is implemented server-side as five named per-field blockers plus a final-confirmation blocker: no suggestion, review required, required value missing, sensitive confirmation missing, and manual signature required. The server re-derives the lifecycle state from persisted rows and refuses independently of what the browser rendered.

meta.title: The export gate is built and enforced on the server
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: web/src/lib/jobs/export-gate.ts:93-136; independent server-side refusal at web/src/app/(app)/fill/[jobId]/review/actions.ts:154-168.

declaration-must-be-typed.text: A declaration or consent field cannot be accepted, because acceptance of a sensitive field is refused outright, yet the export gate requires an ACCEPTED or CORRECTED row for it. The only route through is Save edit: the person types the attestation themselves. The design is deliberate, and it is why an unmatched declaration is classified MISSING rather than UNSUPPORTED.

meta.title: A declaration is only ever satisfied by a person typing it
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: Refusal at web/src/lib/jobs/review-resolution.ts:247-253 (SENSITIVE_ACCEPT_FORBIDDEN); requirement at web/src/lib/jobs/export-gate.ts:93-136 (FIELD_n_SENSITIVE_CONFIRMATION); the MISSING reclassification at web/src/lib/jobs/confidence.ts:24-37, added in commit 54f80ab.

confidence-panel-unwired.text: The confidence display in the review panel is wired to nothing. Overall confidence and the five factor scores exist in the schema and are loaded by the page's query, but the view model never projects them onto the candidate, so every reviewer sees "No overall confidence is available" and five factors reading "Not available".

meta.title: The reviewer is never shown a confidence score
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: Component accepts the fields at web/src/app/(app)/fill/[jobId]/review/review-components.tsx:36-51; only evidence is passed at review-panel.tsx:229-248; the projection is absent at review-view-model.ts:228-243. Data present at web/prisma/schema.prisma:352-353 and :376-381 and loaded at review/page.tsx:81-84.

no-field-overview.text: A reviewer walks the target form strictly one field at a time with Previous and Next. There is no field list, no jump-to-field and no unresolved-items navigator; the only aggregate shown is a raw count of remaining blockers, which includes the final-confirmation blocker among them.

meta.title: A reviewer cannot see the whole form at once
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: Navigation at web/src/app/(app)/fill/[jobId]/review/review-panel.tsx:327-364; the blocker count at review/page.tsx:322-334.

rejection-is-a-decision-not-a-deletion.text: Settling a field writes a REJECTED row for every declined alternative, and a rejected candidate stays visible and re-choosable rather than disappearing. Stepping past a field without pressing an action button is recognised as no decision, so walking the form does not silently overwrite an earlier one.

meta.title: A declined suggestion is recorded, not discarded
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: declineAlternatives at web/src/lib/jobs/review-resolution.ts:203-211; sticky rejected candidates at review-panel.tsx:150-156; the baseline mechanism at review-panel.tsx:84-101 and actions.ts:107-114.

test-session-unreachable-in-production.text: The HMAC test-session cookie is the only authentication bypass in the codebase and it cannot be reached in production. Four independent constraints hold it closed: the secret resolves to null unless APP_ENV is exactly test, boot fails if the secret is set outside test, boot fails if APP_ENV is test while a deployment marker is present, and the enum makes test disjoint from staging and production. It also supplies identity only, never authorisation.

meta.title: The authentication bypass cannot be reached in production
meta.author: assistant
meta.provenance: web/src/lib/auth/test-session.ts:40 and :60; web/src/lib/config/env.ts:140-144 and :154-159; identity-only scope at web/src/lib/authz.ts:53-61.

internal-routes-trust-a-client-header.text: The internal processing and retention routes verify only that K_SERVICE is set and that a request header is present, and both x-cloudtasks-taskname and x-cloudscheduler are client-settable. A Cloud Tasks OIDC token is minted but no application code verifies it. The real protection is Cloud Run IAM, outside the application.

meta.title: The internal routes verify a header, not a token
